headline: High risk of shared-workspace data leakage and capability conflict; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are medium.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes filesystem content and uses diff-based edit proposals, while Replit Agent operates inside a persistent Repl workspace with shell/tool access. If Replit content is copied into Mentat or both touch the same files, attacker-controlled text can be treated as instructions. The shared filesystem bridge makes this plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF files from the Replit workspace are copied into Mentat for editing
IF both agents operate on the same repository checkout without content provenance checks
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Require manual review of any file content before Mentat edits it
Prefix imported text with provenance labels
Use read-only exports for handoff files
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat touches source code and model-provider API keys, and Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. Both have broad network egress and shared filesystem-based state, so sensitive material can flow from one agent’s workspace into the other’s outputs or remote APIs. The blast radius includes secrets and deployment data, making this dangerous by default.
conditions: IF either agent is given files containing secrets or deployment configuration
IF the two agents share a filesystem or copied workspace artifacts
mitigations: Do not place secrets in shared workspaces
Rotate any API keys before cross-agent handoff
Use separate repos or Repls per agent
Redact sensitive files before transfer
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and secret-scanning

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and modify git state, and both support multiple instances. Mentat shares state via filesystem, while Replit Agent persists Repl filesystem across sessions. Concurrent edits to the same repo can race and overwrite each other without locking, which matches the high-severity overlap indicator.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same git branch or directory
IF no external lock or merge gate serializes their writes
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Serialize edits with a simple lock file
Review and merge one agent’s diff before the other runs
Avoid concurrent runs on the same checkout
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and Replit Agent can act inside the Repl with tool calls and user checkpoints. If Replit consumes Mentat’s output as authoritative, an error can cascade into concrete actions. The pair is not fully autonomous, but the handoff path exists in default workflows.
conditions: IF Replit Agent applies Mentat-generated diffs without independent verification
IF Mentat output is used as the sole source for downstream actions
mitigations: Require a second human review of diffs
Compare proposed changes against the original files
Run tests before applying edits
Limit Replit Agent to advisory mode for imported diffs
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat handles model-provider API keys, while Replit Agent handles Replit Secrets store and third-party API keys plus deployment configuration. Even without a named jurisdiction mismatch, the pair can place the same sensitive data class under different retention and handling regimes across two vendors. That creates a compliance mismatch risk in default coding workflows.
conditions: IF the same secret or deployment artifact is processed by both vendors
IF retention or deletion expectations differ between the two environments
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared tasks
Document which vendor stores each secret
Delete temporary artifacts after handoff
Use separate credentials per environment
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
